what: GlobalFoundries manufactures chips designed by other companies. It focuses on specialised process technologies rather than the most advanced nodes: chips for cars, smartphones, internet-of-things devices and defence systems.
customers: Fabless chip designers, carmakers, communications equipment companies and the US government.
money: wafer manufacturing on specialty and mature process technologies
moat: Manufacturing in the United States, Germany and Singapore rather than Taiwan, which customers and governments pay a premium for when supply security matters.
risks: Revenue was flat last year and has fallen about 6% a year over three years
Smartphone and industrial chip demand has been weak
Chinese foundries are adding mature-node capacity and pushing prices down
Factory utilisation drives margins and has been below capacity
opportunities: Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
Cash of about $2.3 billion exceeds its debt
Government funding supports its US and European capacity expansion
watch: Wafer shipments, utilisation and the share of revenue under long-term agreements.
